claim_decisions.statement: IPC's February 2026 analysis classified food insecurity for December 2025–March 2026 across 45 rural districts, citing weather shocks and localized insecurity among several drivers.
claim_decisions.uncertainty: Classification-period estimate informed by September–November 2025 survey and secondary data; not observed outcomes for every month or an October 2026 caseload.

claim_decisions.statement: Source dated 2026-02-18 reports: IPC identifies localized insecurity as a main food-insecurity driver in Kachi and Tank, disrupting livelihoods, markets, services and income.

claim_decisions.reason: Retain bounded source-supported finding with vintage and causal limitations; no extrapolation to 2026 or evaluated impact.
claim_decisions.statement: Source dated 2026-02-18 reports: The household assessment associated drought with income declines of 30% in Balochistan, 14% in Sindh and 9% in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa; respondents also reported water scarcity and reduced crop or livestock production.
claim_decisions.uncertainty: Self-reported survey livelihood/income associations in the assessment period, not a causally attributed climate effect or current provincial income loss.

gaps: Do not infer a climate-to-conflict chain from the overlap of food insecurity, drought/floods and insecurity. Localized Kachi/Tank conflict constraints are independently identified.

executive_assessment.text: Balochistan's policy identifies gendered health-access and rural livelihood barriers, while WHO supplies a dated monsoon response with named service locations.
IPC adds Kachi/Tank livelihood and market constraints from insecurity, with separate drought-related survey findings and limited rural-district coverage.
